newsitem.title: FRANCE: France's Chirac sending message to Middle East.
newsitem.headline: France's Chirac sending message to Middle East.

text.p: French Foreign Minister Herve de Charette said on Sunday he would carry a message from President Jacques Chirac intended to give a boost to stalled peace talks when he visits the Middle East later this week.

"I will certainly arrive with a very strong message from France, from the president, to help facilitate a resumption of the dialogue," de Charette told RMC radio when asked about the goal of his visit.
The minister is visiting Israel, Syria and Lebanon during a three-day trip to the region beginning on Tuesday.
France has been pressing for months for a higher profile for itself and its European partners in Middle East diplomacy, now dominated by the United States.
De Charette said French efforts in the Middle East were intended to complement Washington's role, not rival it.
"We are obviously well acquainted with the U.S. role in that part of the world, where the Americans have vital interests," he said.

"But at the same time we believe that France and Europe also have vital interests in the region...and that we can help in the search for peace and development in this region, in a way that complements that of the United States," he said.
De Charette said on Saturday that he had set up a special team to track Mideast peace developments with an eye to increasing its activities in the region.
While the European Union has agreed to underwrite much of the cost of the peace process, Washington has led negotiations for a political deal.
Israel objects to a mediation role for France as Paris has avidly courted the region's Arab powers.

Israel last week lodged an official complaint after Paris disclosed that de Charette would spend just 24 hours in the Jewish state. Israeli Foreign Ministry spokesman Ygal Palmor said Paris had originally planned "a full state visit of two or three days".
